part.text:
Fixed. The issue was in `StatementIndentationFixer` (src/Fixer/Whitespace/StatementIndentationFixer.php): multiline class constants and properties were treated as separate statements at each comma/keyword, so continuation lines lost their indentation (e.g. `BAR = 'Foo';` after a comma was re-indented to the class level).

The fix gives class member declarations (constants and properties) their own indentation scope:

- Class-body `{` blocks are now tagged (`is_class_body`) when opened after a `class`/`interface`/`trait`/`extends`/`implements` signature (StatementIndentationFixer.php:475, StatementIndentationFixer.php:519).
- When a visibility/`readonly` modifier (or `const`/`var`) is found in a class body, a new helper `findClassMemberEndIndex()` (StatementIndentationFixer.php:828) looks ahead to distinguish constants/properties from methods, and a dedicated scope covering the whole declaration up to `;` is pushed (StatementIndentationFixer.php:611). This normalizes continuation lines to the member indent while keeping array-valued members relatively indented, and fixes comma-separated members.

Verification: all 93 StatementIndentationFixer tests (incl. the 14 previously failing multiline const/property cases) pass, plus BracesFixer (compatibility mode) and all Whitespace fixers; the full suite shows only pre-existing environmental failures (identical on the unmodified tree).
